paths.def: Seronegative spondyloarthropathy (HLA-B27), young men (M:F ≈ 2.5–5:1); axial skeleton + entheses + proximal large joints ("close to the midline, away from the distal extremities").

sx: Symmetric polyarthritis, morning stiffness > 1 h
ex: Stage I: soft tissue swelling, periarticular osteopenia (phalangeal band osteoporosis), widened joint space (effusion)
II: + marginal subchondral erosions, uniform narrowing
III: + bone destruction, subluxations, ulnar deviation, pencil-in-cup
IV: + ankylosis
lab: US/Doppler: synovitis, erosions earlier than X-ray
img: MRI: synovitis, bone oedema (pre-erosive)
tx: US/MRI for early disease
cx: Atlanto-axial subluxation
oth: No osteophytes; bilateral symmetric
paths.def: Chronic inflammatory polyarthritis first involving the small joints of the extremities – symmetric (MCP, PIP, wrists, MTP).

sx: Gout: acute red hot joint; septic: fever, monoarthritis
ex: Gout: juxta-articular punched-out erosions with OVERHANGING sclerotic margins, tophi, normal bone density, preserved joint space until late
Septic arthritis: early normal or periarticular osteoporosis; later rapid joint space narrowing, irregular surfaces, destruction, ANKYLOSIS, osteomyelitis
lab: US: effusion → guided aspiration (diagnostic)
img: MRI septic arthritis positive within 24 h: effusion (T2 hyper), thick enhancing synovium, subchondral oedema, soft tissue abscess; Gout MRI: tophi intermediate T1, effusion hypo T1/hyper T2
tx: Aspiration is key in septic arthritis
cx: Septic arthritis → ankylosis
oth: Ankylosis appears in AS, RA, septic arthritis – never arthrosis
paths.def: Gout: monosodium urate deposition (1st MTP – podagra); septic arthritis: bacterial infection of a joint (emergency).

sx: < 30 y: osteochondroma, NOF, SBC, ABC, osteoid osteoma, chondroblastoma (epiphysis), osteosarcoma, Ewing
> 30 y: metastases, myeloma, lymphoma, chondrosarcoma, giant cell tumour (epiphysis, after physis closure)
ex: Benign: single, sharp sclerotic margin, narrow transition, < 6 cm, homogeneous/trabeculated, intact cortex, no/solid periosteal reaction
Osteoma: dense, facial sinuses/skull; osteoid osteoma: nidus < 1.5 cm with sclerosis, night pain relieved by aspirin
Haemangioma: vertebral body, vertical striations; CT polka-dot; MRI T1 & T2 bright
img: CT: matrix, nidus; MRI: local extension
tx: Radiography first; MRI for local staging
cx: Osteochondroma (metaphysis, exostosis, cortex & marrow continuous with bone) and enchondroma (short bones lytic, long bones sclerotic; Ollier, Maffucci) → chondrosarcoma; giant cell tumour – malignant potential
oth: Classification by tissue: bone, cartilage, connective, vascular, reticulo-endothelial (Ewing), marrow (plasmocytoma), adamantinoma
paths.def: Approach: age, location (epiphysis/metaphysis/diaphysis, central/eccentric), margins, zone of transition, matrix, periosteal reaction, cortex, soft tissue.

sx: Pain, swelling, pathologic fracture
ex: Malignant signs: ill-defined/permeative, wide transition, cortical destruction, aggressive periosteal reaction (lamellated, spiculated, Codman), soft-tissue mass, > 6 cm
Osteosarcoma: metaphysis around the knee, lytic/sclerotic/mixed, sunburst + Codman triangle
Ewing: diaphysis of long bones, permeative, ONION-SKIN (multilamellar) periosteal reaction, large soft-tissue mass
Chondrosarcoma: > 40 y, pelvis/proximal femur/humerus, lysis with "popcorn"/"snowflake" chondroid calcifications
Myeloma: multiple punched-out lytic lesions (skull, axial), diffuse osteopenia; plasmocytoma single
img: MRI: local staging (marrow, skip lesions, soft tissue, joint); CT chest: lung metastases; bone scan/PET: distant
tx: Biopsy after imaging staging
cx: Metastases: lytic (lung, kidney, thyroid), sclerotic (prostate, breast), mixed
oth: Layered onion-bulb periostosis suggests malignant tumour / Ewing
paths.def: Primary (osteosarcoma, Ewing, chondrosarcoma, myeloma) vs secondary (metastases – most frequent bone malignancy in adults).

sx: KUB: opaque stones, calcifications, renal outlines, psoas
ex: IVU: iodinated contrast IV; nephrogram → pyelogram (calyces, pelvis, ureters, bladder); films at 5, 15 min, post-void; irradiates gonads (protection possible)
lab: US: first-line – size (10–12 cm), cortex, hydronephrosis, cysts, stones, bladder; gives no functional information
img: Native CT: stones (most sensitive); 3-phase CT: tumours; CT urography; MRI: iodine allergy, characterisation; scintigraphy: function
tx: Phases: corticomedullary 25–40 s (cortex ≠ medulla), nephrographic 90–100 s, excretory 5–10 min
cx: Left kidney slightly higher and ~1.5 cm longer; T12–L2
oth: Functionally mute kidney on IVU: no contrast at 5 and 15 min
paths.def: KUB, IV urography, retrograde/antegrade pyelography, cystography, US, CT (native, CT urography), MRI, scintigraphy.

sx: Renal colic, haematuria
ex: KUB: radiopaque stones; IVU: delayed nephrogram, dilatation above obstruction
lab: US: hyperechoic focus with acoustic shadow, twinkling artefact, hydronephrosis
img: Native low-dose CT = gold standard (size, location, density)
tx: US in children/pregnancy; CT in adults
cx: Phleboliths (round, central lucency) vs ureteric stone
oth: Large kidney syndrome: renal colic/obstruction
paths.def: Stones (calcium oxalate/phosphate – opaque; uric acid – radiolucent on X-ray but seen on CT) causing colic and hydronephrosis.

paths.n: Renal masses: cysts, RCC, urothelial carcinoma
sx: Haematuria, flank mass, pain (classic triad rare)
ex: IVU: calyceal distortion (RCC), filling defect (urothelial)
lab: Simple cyst: anechoic, thin wall, posterior enhancement; RCC: solid, variable echogenicity, Doppler flow
img: CT = single best method: enhancement > 15–20 HU, staging (renal vein & IVC thrombus, nodes, metastases)
Urothelioma: extension "along the watershed", multicentric, stenosis/obstruction, starts in the sinus, retroperitoneal nodes
tx: Vascular assessment to detect venous tumour thrombus
cx: Angiomyolipoma: macroscopic fat (negative HU)
oth: Bosniak I simple, II minimally complex (thin septa/fine Ca), IIF follow-up, III thick septa/wall (≈ 50 % malignant), IV enhancing soft tissue (malignant)
paths.def: Simple cyst most frequent; Bosniak classification guides management; RCC = solid enhancing cortical mass; urothelial carcinoma from collecting system.

sx: Small: hypoxia/ischaemia (renal artery stenosis), chronic stasis, chronic infection (chronic pyelonephritis – irregular scars; TB), nephrosclerosis, hypoplasia
ex: Large: hypertrophy/hyperplasia, renal colic (obstruction), acute infection (acute pyelonephritis, abscess), renal vein thrombosis, hydronephrosis, polycystic kidney, tumours
lab: Bilateral smooth large: acute tubular necrosis, acute glomerulonephritis, diabetes, amyloidosis, lupus, lymphoma, bilateral obstruction
img: Bumpy irregular unilateral: renal mass; bilateral: ADPKD
tx: US first
cx: ADPKD: bilateral, contrast does not enter cysts; horseshoe kidney: isthmus anterior to aorta
oth: Small kidney NOT produced by renal vein thrombosis, polar tumour, polycystic kidney
paths.def: Change in renal size – unilateral or bilateral, smooth or irregular contour.

sx: Haematuria, flank pain, shock
ex: IVU and plain film have limited value (unstable patient where CT impossible: one-shot IVU)
lab: US limited in trauma (FAST for fluid); transplant: Doppler – renal artery stenosis, fluid collections (lymphocele, urinoma, haematoma), ATN/rejection (RI), obstruction
img: Contrast CT (arterial + nephrographic + excretory) in haemodynamically stable patient; angiography for embolisation
tx: Transplant: CT for lymphoproliferative disease, stones
cx: Urinoma, pseudoaneurysm, AV fistula
oth: AAST I contusion/subcapsular haematoma … V shattered kidney / hilar avulsion
paths.def: Trauma graded by AAST on contrast CT; transplant follow-up mostly by Doppler US.

sx: Haematuria, retention
ex: Compensated stasis (obstruction): detrusor hypertrophy, wall thickening, trabeculation, pseudodiverticula
Decompensated: large atonic thin-walled bladder, diverticula, reflux
lab: US: wall thickness, post-void residue, stones, tumours (non-mobile, vascularised)
img: CT urography / MRI: bladder tumour staging (muscle invasion by MRI)
tx: Cystoscopy remains reference
cx: Blood clot vs tumour: mobility, Doppler flow
oth: Stones: mobile, shadowing
paths.def: Imaging by US, cystography, CT, MRI (tumour staging).

sx: Node groups: retrocrural, para-aortic, paracaval, inter-aortocaval, pelvic
lab: US: lymphadenopathy = enlarged, hypoechoic, round nodes
img: CT method of choice (staging); MRI; PET-CT for lymphoma
tx: Short axis > 10 mm abnormal
cx: Retroperitoneal fibrosis, sarcoma (liposarcoma), haematoma
oth: Stomach, spleen, transverse colon are intraperitoneal
paths.def: Space behind the parietal peritoneum: kidneys, ureters, adrenals, duodenum (D2–D4), pancreas, ascending/descending colon, aorta, IVC, lymph nodes, fat.

sx: Cysts: child post-haemorrhagic; adult lymphangiomas
Haemorrhage: newborn (perinatal stress, heals with calcification), adult (anticoagulants, ACTH, stress, sepsis)
ex: Calcification: post-haemorrhagic, post-TB, cysts
lab: US: first-line; myelolipoma hyperechoic
img: CT method of choice (native then contrast): adenoma < 10 HU, absolute wash-out > 60 %; myelolipoma: macroscopic fat (negative HU) – only specific tumour
MRI chemical shift: signal drop in lipid-rich adenoma
tx: Phaeochromocytoma: non-specific imaging (bright T2), MIBG scintigraphy; negative US does not exclude it
cx: Bilateral masses → metastases (lung cancer); also bilateral phaeo (MEN), hyperplasia
oth: Normal adrenal: Y-shaped, limbs ~5 mm, hypointense to liver on MRI
paths.def: Incidentalomas mostly adenomas; other: myelolipoma, phaeochromocytoma, metastases, carcinoma, neuroblastoma (child), cysts, haemorrhage, hyperplasia.

paths.n: Female genital tract – normal & uterine disease
sx: Endometrium (TVUS): early proliferative thin echogenic line; late proliferative trilaminar; secretory thick hyperechoic homogeneous; post-menopause ≤ 4 mm
ex: MRI T2: endometrium bright, junctional zone dark, myometrium intermediate; cervix & vagina hypo T2
lab: Leiomyoma: hypoechoic well-delineated mass; MRI hypo T1 & T2, necrosis, calcifications
img: Endometrial cancer: post-menopausal bleeding + endometrium > 4 mm → biopsy; MRI: iso T1, hyper T2 vs myometrium; FIGO IA < 50 % myometrium, IB ≥ 50 %, II cervical stroma, III local/nodes, IVA bladder/rectal mucosa
Cervical cancer: MRI local staging (FIGO, parametrial invasion)
tx: Congenital: abnormal fusion of Müllerian ducts – MRI
cx: Adenomyosis: thick junctional zone
oth: CT: myometrium enhances; endometrial collection hypodense (fluid) or hyperdense (blood); ovaries often not seen
paths.def: Transvaginal US first; MRI best for local staging and congenital anomalies; CT for distant disease.

sx: Simple cyst: anechoic, thin wall, posterior enhancement, no flow; MRI hypo T1 / hyper T2
ex: Endometrioma ("chocolate cyst"): homogeneous ground-glass echoes; MRI T1 FatSat bright, T2 shading/intermediate
lab: Malignancy (US): papillary projections, thick vascular septa, solid component, "cyst-in-cyst", ascites; IOTA M1–M5 vs B1–B5
img: MRI: mass > 4 cm, solid enhancing component, wall/septa > 3 mm; CT: peritoneal carcinomatosis (omental caking), nodes, metastases
tx: Simple cyst follow-up by size and menopausal status (< 3 cm done … > 7 cm MRI/surgery)
cx: Dermoid: fat + calcification (tooth)
oth: Role of CT in ovarian cancer: lymph node & distant metastases
paths.def: Functional cysts, endometrioma, dermoid, cystadenomas, malignant epithelial tumours.

sx: BPH: transition zone enlargement; cancer: peripheral zone (70 %)
lab: TRUS: volume, guidance of biopsy; testicular US: tumours hypoechoic, microlithiasis, hydrocele, varicocele, epididymitis (hyperaemia)
img: Multiparametric MRI (T2, DWI, DCE) = modality of choice for detection and local staging (PI-RADS); bone scan/PSMA-PET for metastases
tx: Torsion: clinical diagnosis + Doppler (absent intratesticular flow) – do not delay surgery
cx: Torsion vs epididymitis: absent vs increased flow
oth: Best/most efficient method for the prostate gland: transrectal US (old key); for cancer staging: MRI
paths.def: Prostate imaging: transrectal US, multiparametric MRI; testis: US + Doppler.

sx: Indications: diagnostic (lump, nipple discharge, skin changes) or screening (programmes, high risk, after conservative surgery)
ex: Mammography: CC + MLO views; screening from 40–50 y; limited in dense breasts and implants
lab: US: < 30 y, pregnancy/lactation, dense breast, palpable mass, cyst vs solid, guidance
img: MRI: BRCA/high risk, implants, extent/multifocality, occult primary, neoadjuvant response
tx: BI-RADS 0 incomplete; 1 negative; 2 benign; 3 probably benign – short-interval follow-up; 4 suspicious – biopsy; 5 highly suggestive; 6 proven malignancy
cx: Breast US not first-line > 50 y; follow-up of treated cancer = mammography
oth: Dense breast and augmented breast reduce mammographic sensitivity
paths.def: Mammography, ultrasound, MRI, image-guided biopsy; reports use BI-RADS.

sx: Malignant mammography: spiculated/irregular mass, high density, pleomorphic, fine-linear branching or segmental microcalcifications, architectural distortion, skin thickening, nipple retraction
ex: Benign: round/oval circumscribed mass, coarse popcorn (fibroadenoma), rim/eggshell, vascular calcifications, fat-containing (lipoma, hamartoma)
lab: US malignant: irregular, taller-than-wide, hypoechoic, posterior shadowing, angular margins; benign: oval, parallel, circumscribed; simple cyst anechoic with enhancement
img: MRI malignant: irregular mass, washout (type III) kinetic curve
tx: Core biopsy under US or stereotactic guidance
cx: Fibroadenoma (young women), cysts (40–50 y), phyllodes
oth: Inflammatory carcinoma: skin thickening, oedema
paths.def: Imaging signs guiding BI-RADS category.

sx: Pneumoperitoneum: crescent of air under the diaphragm (erect), Rigler sign (both sides of bowel wall), football sign
ex: Bowel obstruction: air-fluid levels – small bowel (central, wider than high, valvulae conniventes) vs colon (peripheral, haustra)
lab: US: free fluid, appendicitis, cholecystitis
img: CT: method of choice for acute abdomen (free air on lung window)
tx: Contrast not mandatory for pneumoperitoneum or occlusion
cx: Apple core sign = colon carcinoma (barium)
oth: Opaque stones visible: renal (most), gallstones (~15 %)
paths.def: Erect/supine abdominal film and chest film.

sx: Indications: chronic conditions, post-operative assessment, findings on other exams; CI: perforation (use water-soluble iodine), acute inflammation
ex: Achalasia: megaoesophagus, air-fluid level with barium sedimentation, ABSENT gastric air bubble, short tapered "bird's beak"
Benign stricture: axial, regular, progressive; malignant: eccentric, irregular, abrupt shoulders, filling defects
lab: Gastric ulcer: addition image (niche) – benign if projecting beyond the wall, Hampton line, smooth converging folds, lesser curvature
img: Cancer: subtraction image (filling defect), rigid wall, interrupted folds
tx: Endoscopy confirms
cx: Diverticula = addition images with mucosal folds
oth: Barium highly diluted possible; never in perforation
paths.def: Contrast (barium) swallow/meal for morphology and motility.

sx: Diffuse: steatosis (bright liver), fibrosis (hyperechoic, coarse), acute hepatitis & congestion (hypoechoic)
ex: Haemangioma: hyperechoic, well defined; CT/MRI peripheral nodular (globular) enhancement with centripetal fill-in; T2 very bright; no biopsy
lab: FNH: central scar, arterial enhancement, iso later; adenoma: young woman on OCP, fat, bleeding
img: HCC (cirrhosis): arterial wash-in + portal/delayed wash-out; metastases: most frequent malignant lesion in non-cirrhotic liver – multiple, hypovascular (portal phase), may be cystic, "target"
Simple cyst: anechoic (US), black on T1, bright T2, 0–20 HU on CT
tx: Primovist MRI: HCC/FNH/adenoma, small metastases, biliary leaks
cx: Lesions not always seen in portal phase; small lesions can be missed
oth: Lesions can be hypo-, hyper- or isodense
paths.def: US for screening; multiphasic CT/MRI for characterisation.

sx: Normal: intrahepatic ducts < 2 mm, CBD ≤ 6–7 mm, gallbladder wall ≤ 3–4 mm, gallbladder up to ~4 cm wide
ex: Gallstones (US): hyperechoic, mobile, posterior acoustic shadow; may fill gallbladder or impact in infundibulum; CT shows only calcified stones
lab: Obstructive jaundice: pancreatic head tumours, cholangiocarcinoma, stones; distal CBD often hidden by gas on US
img: Pancreatitis: contrast CT (Balthazar/CTSI), necrosis, collections; chronic: calcifications, moniliform Wirsung, atrophy or focal enlargement (mimics carcinoma)
Pancreatic carcinoma: hypodense ill-defined head mass, double duct sign, vascular invasion, nodes/liver metastases
MRI/MRCP: ducts, lesions unclear on US/CT, iodine allergy
tx: Emergency CT in pancreatitis: IV access, native + contrast phases
cx: Cystic pancreatic lesions: well delineated – not typical of adenocarcinoma
oth: On MRCP stones are hypointense
paths.def: US first for gallbladder and duct dilatation; CT/MRCP for level and cause; EUS for small stones/tumours.

o.t: It is mandatory in the suspicion of pneumoperitoneum

o.e: Characterisation of a liver nodule needs multiphase contrast CT

Do not require contrast i.v. for characterization

Spiculated ("sunburst") periostosis is also possible in Ewing (book p.140)

Transverse colon is intraperitoneal (ascending & descending are retroperitoneal)

Myelolipoma: fat → hyperechoic on US, hypodense (negative HU) on CT

The adrenal myelolipoma has negative densities on CT

Are parallel to the vertebral body

Cancer usually occurs within 1–2 years after exposure to ionizing radiation
Skin carcinoma can occur after interventional radiology procedures
Children are more sensitive than adults to stochastic effects of ionizing radiation

questions.note: With modern radioprotection radiologists have no significant excess cancer risk; deterministic effects need high doses (interventional, not diagnostic CT); radiation-induced cancers appear after years–decades (leukaemia ~5–10 y, solid tumours > 10 y).

cards.q: Benign bone tumour on X-ray (6 criteria)?
cards.a: Unique (sometimes 2–3), good sclerotic contour, < 6 cm, homogeneous/trabeculated, bone contour intact (or ordostosis), periosteum no/slow modelling.

cards.q: Malignant bone tumour on X-ray (6 criteria)?
cards.a: Unique or multiple, blurred/invasive contour, > 6 cm, anarchic structure, bone contour interrupted/invaded, periosteum spicules/striations/spur.

cards.q: Septic arthritis – early vs late imaging?
cards.a: Early: X-ray often normal (± periarticular osteoporosis); MRI positive within 24 h (fluid, thick vascular synovium, subchondral oedema, fat oedema ± abscess). Late X-ray: narrowing, irregular surface, sclerosis, collapse, ankylosis, osteomyelitis.

cards.q: Which disease can produce bone ankylosis?
cards.a: Only arthritis (AS, RA, septic) – NEVER arthrosis.

cards.q: Size anomalies of bone (congenital vs acquired)?
cards.a: Congenital: aplasia/agenesis, hypoplasia, hyperplasia. Acquired: anostosis (destruction), hypostosis (thinner), hyperostosis (thicker – osteosclerosis or periostosis).
